title: Security, Identity & Trust Architecture
summary: Design secure applications from browser/session mechanics through federated identity, authorization, cryptography, service identity and software supply chain.

modules.title: Security principles & attack surfaces
modules.summary: Develop a threat-oriented mental model before memorizing vulnerability lists.
modules.why: Security is about assets, trust and attacker capabilities across the whole system lifecycle.

units.title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability & authenticity
units.summary: Use core security properties to state what must be protected.
units.challenge: Classify security requirements for login, file upload and audit logging.
units.evidence: Asset/property matrix with consequences of compromise.

units.title: Attack surface, trust boundaries & attacker models
units.summary: Identify where untrusted input and privilege cross boundaries.
units.challenge: Mark trust boundaries on the capstone architecture and enumerate attacker entry points.
units.evidence: Annotated data-flow diagram with attack surfaces.

units.title: Secure design principles
units.summary: Apply least privilege, fail-safe defaults and compartmentalization at architecture level.
units.challenge: Review an over-privileged architecture and redesign blast-radius boundaries.
units.evidence: Architecture review showing reduced privileges and failure impact.

modules.title: Web & application vulnerability engineering
modules.summary: Understand common vulnerability mechanics deeply enough to exploit and prevent them.
modules.why: Developers need concrete attacker intuition, not checklist-only awareness.

units.title: SQL/command/template injection & unsafe deserialization
units.summary: Understand data/code boundary failures and parameterization.
units.challenge: Exploit and fix injection vulnerabilities in a local lab.
units.evidence: Exploit proof plus code/query changes that remove the injection primitive.

units.title: XSS & CSRF
units.summary: Understand browser-origin credential and script-execution attacks.
units.challenge: Exploit a local XSS and CSRF flow, then implement layered mitigations.
units.evidence: Attack sequence and mitigation mapping.

units.title: SSRF, path traversal & file-upload attacks
units.summary: Protect server-side network/filesystem capabilities from untrusted input.
units.challenge: Threat-model an image import/file upload service and build protective boundaries.
units.evidence: Abuse-case test suite and architecture mitigations.

units.title: Broken access control & object authorization
units.summary: Prevent users from acting on resources merely because they can name them.
units.challenge: Create privilege-escalation tests across tenant/project/task boundaries.
units.evidence: Authorization matrix and negative test suite.

modules.title: Authentication & account lifecycle
modules.summary: Secure registration, login, MFA, recovery and device/session history as one lifecycle.
modules.why: Attackers target recovery, enrollment and reset flows as much as login itself.

units.title: Password authentication & credential storage
units.summary: Store and verify passwords using adaptive password hashing and abuse controls.
units.challenge: Implement password authentication with realistic brute-force and enumeration protections.
units.evidence: Threat tests and password-storage configuration rationale.

units.title: MFA, passkeys & WebAuthn
units.summary: Add phishing-resistant and step-up authentication deliberately.
units.challenge: Design password+MFA and passkey-first flows for the same product.
units.evidence: Flow diagrams comparing phishing resistance and recovery complexity.

units.title: Verification, password reset & account recovery
units.summary: Treat recovery as a high-privilege authentication ceremony.
units.challenge: Threat-model account recovery including compromised email and malicious support requests.
units.evidence: Recovery policy with escalation/notification/audit controls.

modules.title: Sessions, cookies & login state
modules.summary: Design stateful login sessions that can be rotated, revoked and synchronized across devices/tabs.
modules.why: Sessions are security-sensitive distributed state, not just a cookie value.

units.title: Session IDs & secure cookie transport
units.summary: Keep session secrets unguessable and constrained in browser transport.
units.challenge: Configure session cookies for same-site SPA/API and document each attribute.
units.evidence: Browser/network inspection and attack implications.

units.title: Rotation, fixation & privilege changes
units.summary: Rotate session identity when authentication/privilege context changes.
units.challenge: Demonstrate a fixation-vulnerable flow then fix it with rotation.
units.evidence: Attack/fix trace and tests.

units.title: Distributed sessions, revocation & multi-device control
units.summary: Operate session state across a fleet while supporting logout and device management.
units.challenge: Design session management across 100 app instances with instant user-initiated revocation.
units.evidence: Session data model and failover/revocation behaviour.

modules.title: Bearer tokens, JWTs & refresh-token lifecycle
modules.summary: Understand stateless token trade-offs and the operational problem of revocation.
modules.why: JWTs move state and verification assumptions; they do not eliminate session/security complexity.

units.title: JWT structure, signing & validation
units.summary: Validate issuer, audience, time and algorithm assumptions correctly.
units.challenge: Validate tokens from a rotating-key issuer and reject malformed claim combinations.
units.evidence: Validation policy and negative tests.

units.title: Access & refresh token design
units.summary: Separate short-lived API access from longer-lived reauthentication capability.
units.challenge: Implement refresh-token rotation with theft/reuse detection in a test system.
units.evidence: Token-family state model and theft scenario tests.

units.title: Token revocation & statelessness trade-offs
units.summary: Choose revocation latency and state deliberately.
units.challenge: Compare stateless JWT, opaque token/introspection and server session for three product contexts.
units.evidence: Decision matrix with breach/logout/scale implications.

modules.title: OAuth 2.x, OpenID Connect & SAML federation
modules.summary: Understand delegated authorization, login federation and enterprise SSO as separate protocols/problems.
modules.why: Confusing OAuth with authentication is a common source of insecure architecture.

units.title: OAuth roles, authorization code & PKCE
units.summary: Trace delegated authorization through browser/client/authorization server/resource server.
units.challenge: Trace and implement a test authorization-code+PKCE flow.
units.evidence: Sequence diagram labeling every credential and attacker boundary.

units.title: OIDC login, ID tokens & discovery
units.summary: Layer authentication claims on OAuth safely.
units.challenge: Integrate an OIDC provider and validate issuer/audience/nonce/key rotation.
units.evidence: Login trust model and token-validation tests.

units.title: SAML, enterprise federation & provisioning concepts
units.summary: Understand enterprise SSO and lifecycle concerns beyond OIDC.
units.challenge: Design enterprise SSO onboarding supporting OIDC and SAML customers with role provisioning.
units.evidence: Protocol-neutral identity architecture and mapping policy.

modules.title: Authorization: RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC & policy engines
modules.summary: Model who can do what to which resource under tenant/context constraints.
modules.why: Authorization complexity grows with products; a single role column rarely survives real requirements.

units.title: RBAC, permissions & role hierarchies
units.summary: Separate permissions from roles and model reusable job-function bundles.
units.challenge: Design org/project roles without hard-coding authorization in controllers.
units.evidence: Permission catalog and role mapping.

units.title: ABAC & policy-based authorization
units.summary: Evaluate user/resource/environment attributes for contextual decisions.
units.challenge: Add policies for resource classification, time/device risk and tenant policy.
units.evidence: Policy examples and decision tests.

units.title: Relationship-based authorization
units.summary: Model permissions derived from graph relationships and sharing.
units.challenge: Design Google-Drive-like sharing for folders/files/groups.
units.evidence: Relationship model, check algorithm and revocation semantics.

units.title: Authorization enforcement architecture
units.summary: Place checks consistently across UI, API, service and data boundaries.
units.challenge: Design centralized policy with local enforcement for multi-service SaaS.
units.evidence: Authorization sequence and bypass analysis.

modules.title: Browser security model & cross-origin controls
modules.summary: Understand how origins, credentials, scripts and embeds interact.
modules.why: Browser security controls are architecture constraints for sessions, APIs and integrations.

units.title: Same-origin policy & CORS
units.summary: Distinguish browser read restrictions from server authorization.
units.challenge: Configure a multi-origin frontend/API and demonstrate why CORS is not access control.
units.evidence: Browser tests for allowed/blocked origins and credential modes.

units.title: CSP, SRI & framing controls
units.summary: Reduce script injection and third-party resource risk.
units.challenge: Deploy a strict CSP to an app with third-party dependencies and remove unsafe-inline.
units.evidence: CSP policy and violation report analysis.

units.title: postMessage, iframes & embedded-app trust
units.summary: Secure intentional cross-origin communication.
units.challenge: Build a secure embedded widget communicating with a host page.
units.evidence: Threat model and message validation tests.

modules.title: Applied cryptography, PKI & key management
modules.summary: Use cryptographic primitives through safe high-level systems and understand trust/key lifecycle.
modules.why: Engineers should not invent cryptography, but must understand what primitives guarantee and how keys fail operationally.

units.title: Hashing, MACs, symmetric/asymmetric encryption & signatures
units.summary: Distinguish primitive purposes and misuse modes.
units.challenge: Map ten security requirements to the correct primitive and identify common misuse.
units.evidence: Primitive/property decision table.

units.title: PKI, certificates & certificate lifecycle
units.summary: Understand how identities bind to public keys and how trust is rotated/revoked.
units.challenge: Build a small local CA/client/server certificate chain and rotate one certificate.
units.evidence: Trust-chain diagram and rotation procedure.

units.title: KMS/HSM & envelope encryption
units.summary: Separate data encryption keys from key-encryption/master keys and audit usage.
units.challenge: Design encryption at rest for tenant secrets with rotation and compromise response.
units.evidence: Key hierarchy and lifecycle runbook.

modules.title: Secrets, IAM & workload identity
modules.summary: Authenticate machines/services without static credentials scattered through configuration.
modules.why: Service-to-service trust and secret lifecycle determine blast radius in cloud-native systems.

units.title: Secret storage, injection & rotation
units.summary: Keep credentials out of source/images and rotate without outage.
units.challenge: Replace static DB/API secrets with managed retrieval and rotation.
units.evidence: Secret lifecycle diagram and rotation test.

units.title: IAM roles, policies & least privilege
units.summary: Grant workloads narrowly scoped capabilities with auditable identities.
units.challenge: Reduce a wildcard cloud role to least privilege using observed accesses.
units.evidence: Policy before/after and denied-action tests.

units.title: Workload identity & service-to-service mTLS
units.summary: Issue verifiable identities to workloads and authorize service calls independently of network location.
units.challenge: Design service identity for dynamic Kubernetes workloads with no long-lived shared secret.
units.evidence: Trust/issuance/rotation architecture.

modules.title: Threat modeling & secure architecture reviews
modules.summary: Find abuse paths before implementation and turn them into testable security requirements.
modules.why: Security review is most effective when architectural choices are still changeable.

units.title: Data-flow diagrams & STRIDE
units.summary: Systematically enumerate threats at process/data-flow/store boundaries.
units.challenge: Threat-model login, file upload and async notification flows.
units.evidence: DFDs with ranked threats and mitigations.

units.title: Abuse cases & risk prioritization
units.summary: Model attacker goals and prioritize by likelihood/impact/exposure.
units.challenge: Create abuse stories for tenant admin, malicious member and external attacker.
units.evidence: Risk register with rationale and owners.

units.title: Security architecture review & verification
units.summary: Turn threat models into requirements, tests and release gates.
units.challenge: Define a lightweight security review process for feature teams.
units.evidence: Review template and gate criteria.

modules.title: Software supply-chain & dependency security
modules.summary: Protect source, builds, dependencies, artifacts and deployment provenance.
modules.why: An application can be secure and still compromised through its build/dependency chain.

units.title: Dependencies, vulnerabilities & SBOMs
units.summary: Know what code you ship and respond to vulnerable components quickly.
units.challenge: Generate dependency inventory and respond to a simulated critical transitive vulnerability.
units.evidence: Remediation decision log and SBOM artifact.

units.title: Build provenance & artifact signing
units.summary: Establish confidence that artifacts came from expected source/build processes.
units.challenge: Design CI so production accepts only signed/attested artifacts.
units.evidence: Supply-chain trust diagram and policy gates.

units.title: CI security & source-control protections
units.summary: Protect high-privilege automation from untrusted code and credential theft.
units.challenge: Threat-model a CI pipeline executing pull-request code with deployment credentials.
units.evidence: Hardened pipeline policy and attack-path reductions.

modules.title: Data security, privacy & audit architecture
modules.summary: Classify sensitive data, minimize collection and produce trustworthy access/change evidence.
modules.why: Product architecture must encode privacy, retention, residency and audit obligations—not bolt them on later.

units.title: Data classification & minimization
units.summary: Know what sensitive data exists, why it exists and where it flows.
units.challenge: Inventory capstone data and remove/shorten retention for unnecessary sensitive fields.
units.evidence: Data inventory with owner, purpose, retention and protection class.

units.title: Tenant/user data isolation & residency
units.summary: Enforce logical/physical boundaries and regional constraints across services/stores.
units.challenge: Design regulated tenant storage while shared compute serves other tenants.
units.evidence: Data-flow/residency architecture and isolation tests.

units.title: Security audit logs & tamper evidence
units.summary: Capture who did what, to which resource, when and from what security context.
units.challenge: Design audit logging for role changes and sensitive downloads without leaking secrets.
units.evidence: Audit event schema and sample investigation trail.
